summary.text: Brad Tschida is the Republican candidate for Montana State Senate District 49 in the November 3, 2026 general election, facing incumbent Democrat Willis Curdy.
A former Republican member of the Montana House of Representatives who represented District 97 from 2015 to 2023, he lost to Curdy in the 2022 Senate race.

paragraphs.text: Brad Tschida took office in the Montana House of Representatives on January 5, 2015, succeeding Democrat Todd Mowbray, and left office on January 2, 2023.
Ballotpedia lists his profession as salesman, educator and business owner.
He won re-election to House District 97 in 2016, 2018 and 2020, and did not run for re-election to the House in 2022.

Tschida’s committee assignments included the Appropriations and Rules committees, and he was listed as chair of General Government in the 2017 session; in 2021-2022 he was vice chair of Appropriations.
In 2022 he defeated Nancy Burgoyne in the Republican primary for Senate District 49 and lost the general election to Willis Curdy.
He advanced from the Republican primary for the same seat on June 2, 2026.
